name: William H. Merrifield
role: Partner in Ferris & Merrifield, managers of Roosevelt's Maltese Cross ranch
bio: William H. (Bill) Merrifield was a partner in Ferris & Merrifield, managers of the Maltese Cross (Chimney Butte) ranch seven miles up the Little Missouri from Medora. In March 1884 he sat on the committee that drafted by-laws for the Bad Lands stockmen's association. In June 1884 the paper noted that Theodore Roosevelt, the future president, then a New York assemblyman, was staying at Ferris & Merrifield's ranch, and that summer the firm shipped in a thousand head of cattle; Merrifield went east to buy more in March 1885 and brought back Elkhorn and Chimney Butte cattle that May. He and the Ferris brothers hosted dances and parties at the ranch, including a Thanksgiving dance in 1885. In January 1886 he and Sylvane Ferris went to Chicago at Roosevelt's invitation, and a report that he had married on the trip was later retracted as a made-up story. In August and September 1886 he hunted with Roosevelt in the Bull River mountains for a white goat, and that October Roosevelt turned the Elkhorn brand over to Ferris & Merrifield before Merrifield shipped cattle to Chicago and went home to Canada for the winter.
